report:
PASS certifies only the explicitly limited radial A–G theorem, including its nonnegative-density extension. The historical original-S06 assessment remains INCONCLUSIVE and is not replaced. original_S06_completed=false; weighted_extremals_unresolved=true. The supplied independent candidate flag remains true, with scope limited to A–G.

I independently reconstructed the current article, the historical positive-density argument, the density-zero supplement, and all eight supplied proof notes. The namespaced dependencies S06-radial-zeros-blind/n1–n8 form an acyclic chain with valid references. Their mathematical deductions agree with the article after the expressly identified changes for nonnegative densities. Prior verdicts, numerical observations, hashes, reading flags, and artifact metadata provide no premise for this verdict.

The mathematical foundations used fall within the task’s explicit permission. I freshly opened and checked [Demailly, I.5.1–5.9, pp. 39–40](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf) and [BGL, Section 2.1, including Proposition 2.1 and its complete proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090). Demailly’s decreasing-limit application is valid: the radial caps are psh, decrease, remain finite away from the center, and converge to the stated canonical pole. Semipositive Hessians suffice. BGL’s bounded corrected expansion and locality apply without closed backgrounds; its positivity statement requires nonnegative currents, which every relevant truncation has. Section 2.2 explicitly assumes BMP and is never used here. The sole listed external claim records n1’s source-convention assertion, independently confirmed in the publisher’s primary text. Positive covariance, replacing u by u/γ when D_source=γD_task, also verifies the application without guessing a convention.

The foundation calculations in n1 are correct. For a radial local potential Φ and Q=rΦ′, the complex Hessian has eigenvalues Q/r and Q′. In the task convention, polar integration gives radial mass kQ^(k−1)Q′dr=d(Q^k); hence κ^k has radial mass d(P^k), P=r/(1+r), and total mass one. Projection pullbacks commute with bounded corrected products by local decreasing smooth approximation. Dimensionally excessive terms vanish. For closed positive h and bounded h-psh b, the bounded-product recursion gives (h+dd^c b)^m−h^m=dd^c[b∑_{j=0}^{m−1}(h+dd^c b)^j∧h^(m−1−j)]. Compact Stokes therefore proves the bounded mass invariance used in F. This does not assume global smooth approximation preserving a nonclosed Hermitian background.

A is established. The displayed Qα and its derivative are correct, and dQα/dP>0 because T≥1 and 0<α<1. Its endpoints are zero and one. The homogeneous expression for P proves smoothness away from o, including the entire hyperplane; the density there has value 1−α>0. Local radial caps establish the genuine κ-psh representative with uα(o)=−∞. Bounded truncation locality identifies the non-pluripolar measure off o; its extension by zero has mass one, with no additional hyperplane or pole measure. Near o, qα is asymptotic to α^k(1−α)r^(−k)L^(−1−k(1−α)). Multiplication by the smooth radial volume proves L¹ integrability and divergence of every Lᵖ integral for p>1. Different α have unbounded differences, hence distinct ordinary types. The integral ∫exp(−kL+tL^α)dL converges for every finite t>0, proving trivial multiplier ideals with the specified convention. Ordinary equivalence transfers this ideal conclusion to U.

One harmless wording clarification is necessary in A: “It is L1 and no Lp” means the density qα. The potential uα itself belongs to every finite Lᵖ. The current article and n2 make that intended subject unambiguous. No model assertion follows or is used.

B is established for q≥0. Shrinking the pole neighborhood makes q≥qα/2 there, so M(r)>0 at every positive radius. Thus Q=M^(1/k) is smooth even where q vanishes, and Q′≥0. The inverse U′=(Q−P)/r defines the solution. Smooth radial extension at infinity gives a smooth profile in t=1/r: rotational invariance on a transverse complex line yields a smooth function of its squared modulus. Probability normalization gives M(t)=1−k∫_0^t q(v)(1+v)^(−k−1)dv. Consequently Q(0)=P(0)=1 in that coordinate, and −(Q−P)/t is smooth. This proves convergence of the normalization integral, value zero on the whole hyperplane, and smoothness there even at density zeros. The radial Hessian is semipositive, and the central residual estimate gives the genuine sole pole. Strict-superlevel truncation restrictions equal qκ^k there and increase to that explicitly integrable measure, proving its actual mass one.

The ordinary equivalence and exact stretching membership are valid globally. The residual extends continuously and is bounded on projective space. With a*=inf R, v_t=uα+t a* is genuinely κ-psh and t^(−1)v_t+(1−t^(−1))uα=uα+a*≤U. Both sides have the required −∞ value at the common pole; at t=1 the zero-coefficient term is omitted. This proves precisely the stated stretching definition. Radial uniqueness uses k≥2 to ensure nonnegative flux: the equation gives (Q_V^k)′=M′, zero central flux removes the integration constant, and the positive root fixes V′. Normalization fixes the remaining additive constant. No nonsymmetric uniqueness or envelope identity is inferred.

C is established without differentiating the density error. Writing b=k(1−α), central integration gives M−Qα^k=O(r^δL^(−b−1)), and therefore (M−Qα^k)/Qα^k=O(r^δ/L). The positive-root expansion gives Δ=Q−Qα=O(r^δL^(α−2)). The exact identity Q′/Qα′=(q/qα)(Qα/Q)^(k−1) gives Δ′=O(r^(δ−1)L^(α−2)). Integrating R′=Δ/r and using R″=Δ′/r−Δ/r² proves all three claimed bounds and the finite residual limit. In real coordinates, ∇R=2R′z and D²R=2R′I+4R″z⊗z. These give Hölder exponent min(1,2δ). At δ=1/2 the gradient tends to zero and R−R0=o(|z|); at δ=1 the Hessian tends to zero and ∇R=o(|z|). Thus both critical endpoint extensions, including their zero derivatives, are valid. Only R crosses the pole.

D is established by both supplied reconstructions. In logarithmic coordinates all derivatives of the baseline flux and its reciprocal have at most polynomial growth. Every weighted derivative of g decays faster than any exponential rate there. The central error integral, its derivatives, division by the baseline mass, and positive-root composition preserve that decay. Integrating the flux difference proves the same for R−R0. Conversion to ordinary radial derivatives introduces only finite inverse powers of r, absorbed by arbitrarily strong decay. Extension by zero is smooth and flat; composition with |z|² proves the asserted spatial flatness. Determinant decay alone is not substituted for this hypothesis.

E is established. The cutoff integrals are finite and positive; their ratio cancels the total perturbation mass exactly. Small positive c keeps the density positive, and finite cutoff support preserves smoothness at infinity. Near o the central error is exactly c∫_0^r s^δ(Qα^k)′ds. Substitution s=re^(−y), dominated convergence, and the root expansion give precisely the constants cα(1−α)/δ in R_c′ and cα(1−α)/δ² in R_c−R_c(0). The gradient 2√r R_c′ diverges below δ=1/2; a tangential real Hessian eigenvalue 2R_c′ diverges below δ=1. The residual-to-distance quotient diverges for every Hölder exponent greater than 2δ when 2δ<1. Annular compensation cannot change these central conclusions. Replacing r^δ by exp(−1/r) gives a nonzero balanced perturbation whose every Euler derivative is flat; its central flux difference is positive, so this is an actual nonconstant example of D.

G is established, including hyperplane zeros. Smoothness follows from positive cumulative mass and the probability endpoint, not from smooth density alone. The compact zero-annulus construction is valid. Explicitly, use the smooth step σ from n5 and set ηa(r)=σ(2(r−1))[1−σ(2(r−7/2))], with ηb a nonzero nonnegative smooth bump supported in (5,6). Then ηa is supported in [1,4] and equals one on [3/2,7/2]. Set B=∫ηa qακ^k/∫ηb qακ^k and q0=qα(1−ηa+Bηb). The multiplier is nonnegative, the integral is exactly one, and q0 vanishes on 3/2<r<7/2 while equaling qα near o and infinity. It remains L¹ and belongs to no Lᵖ for p>1. Near o its cumulative mass equals Qα^k exactly, so R′=0. The residual extends constantly there and smoothly everywhere else, including the zero annulus. This independently verifies the article’s equivalent h-and-compensation construction.

F is established only under its antecedent. For the pullback U, bounded corrected-product expansion leaves exactly binomial(m+k,m)h0^m∧(κ+dd^c U_j)^k. Restriction to {U>−j} removes level-boundary contributions and equals the explicit smooth off-pole measure. These restrictions increase to binomial(m+k,m)h0^m∧qκ^k extended by zero across X0×{o}, with finite mass binomial(m+k,m)V0. This proves this particular truncation limit without BMP. Bounded factor potentials with masses tending to zero pull back with that same binomial multiplier; positivity proves v_minus(H)=0. Closed h0 would contradict bounded Stokes mass invariance, and dH=pr0*dh0 proves genuine nonclosedness. Ordinary equivalence, stretching competitors, and transverse residual regularity pull back canonically. No factor existence, unconditional nonclosed example, or singularity-volume threshold is obtained; the displayed raw mass is not an infimum or supremum over an unbounded type.

The historical strictly positive proof does not by itself certify G; the supplement supplies the substantive positive-cumulative-mass argument, which checks out. The remaining assertions of n8 correctly delimit scope. The weighted ideal operator retains the task’s all-t multiplier-ideal inclusion and quasi-everywhere obstacle definition, but receives no regularity result. Failure of Lᵖ does not establish failure of every density-in-capacity regime. General prescribed types, nonsymmetric uniqueness, general density zeros, singular envelopes, and weighted extremals remain unresolved. No priority claim is certified.
